Back: Any organized collection of related information (e.g., phonebook, shopping list, or company orders database)
Software used to create, manage, secure, and query databases (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
Software storing data in related tables, queried with SQL (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server)
Non-relational database storing flexible formats like documents, key-value pairs, or graphs (e.g., MongoDB, DynamoDB, Firebase)
Structured grid of rows and columns representing a real-world category (e.g., orders, customers, employees)
One single horizontal instance or entry of an entity in a table (e.g., Order #101 placed by Rahul in Delhi)
One specific vertical attribute with an enforced data type (e.g., city as VARCHAR, price as DECIMAL, order_date as DATE)
Unique, non-null identifier of each row in a table; only one PK per table (e.g., order_id = 101 in orders)
Primary key with no real-world meaning, generated purely as an ID (e.g., auto-incremented emp_id = 1, 2, 3)
Primary key with real-world meaning or purpose (e.g., SSN, vehicle VIN, book ISBN)
Column in one table referencing another table's primary key to link them (e.g., orders.customer_id -> customers.customer_id)
Primary key formed by combining two or more columns when one column isn't unique alone (e.g., (emp_id, client_id) in works_with)
The four core database operations: Create (INSERT), Read (SELECT), Update (UPDATE), Delete (DELETE)
Online Transaction Processing: many fast, small reads/writes running day-to-day business (e.g., placing an e-commerce order)
Online Analytical Processing: heavy analytical reads over historical data supporting decisions (e.g., 5-year monthly sales trend)
Data Query Language: retrieves data from tables (e.g., SELECT name, city FROM customers;)
Data Manipulation Language: modifies data inside tables (e.g., INSERT INTO, UPDATE, DELETE)
Data Definition Language: defines or changes table/database structure (e.g., CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, DROP TABLE)
Data Control Language: manages user access and permissions (e.g., GRANT SELECT ON orders TO analyst;)
Transaction Control Language: manages and safeguards transactions (e.g., COMMIT; ROLLBACK;)
Atomicity (all-or-nothing transfer), Consistency (rules/types hold), Isolation (concurrent users don't clash), Durability (committed data survives crash)
Data = raw unorganized facts (4999, 'Delhi', 12-Oct); Information = data with context ('Delhi sales were ₹4,999 on 12 Oct')
Organizing data into separate related tables to eliminate duplicate rows and inconsistency (e.g., storing customer city once in customers instead of repeating it in orders)
